motivation: An additive score offset leaves candidate ordering and improvements unchanged but changes the current fixed-relative reward. This algebraic property is distinct from empirical evidence of better policies.
candidate_change: Replace only allocation credit with bounded improvement normalized by recent nonzero improvement magnitudes; derive any noise gate from repeated public-case measurements. Keep trigger, parents, proposals, writer prompts, ordinary selection, evaluator and budgets fixed.
required_properties: Positive affine score transformations preserve credit apart from floating-point effects
Failed evaluations still consume allocation cost
All-zero gains yield zero credit without division by zero
Scale uses only measurements available when credit is assigned
Repeated-source timing variability is assessed before crediting tiny gains
gates_before_launch: Inspect scheduled public-case rereads for timing variability
Specify estimator window, cold start and noise gate before new runs
Check remaining authorized cumulative budget; do not increase cap
limits: Not a claim of novelty or superiority. No numerical formula selected yet because noise evidence is incomplete. No held-out data accessed.

later_development_evidence.implication: Large improvements are possible on AHC024. A sparse1% reward during early plateau is not by itself proof of a bad policy; ignoring tiny incumbent gains may also preserve exploration. Lowering the threshold can change that balance and must be tested as an ablation, not assumed beneficial.

implementation_confound_check.observation: Generated programs differ in reachable moves and annealing acceptance, not only framework allocation. The AHC024 compared SA branches each received four productive follow-ups.
implementation_confound_check.consequence: Do not bundle reward changes with planner/writer changes. A credit-only ablation must keep existing parents, proposal prompts and branch rules fixed; independent runs still require multiple seeds because future histories diverge. A component-level generated-code ablation addresses a different causal question.

latest_credit_evidence.interpretation: Four completed AHC024 adaptive runs have no1% credit, whereas AHC058 has usable positive credit and one adaptive seed wins all controls. This motivates a general score-scale/credit ablation after scheduled noise rereads, not a task-specific switch or an immediate change. The large ModifiedMolt AHC024 breakthrough remains a counterexample to concluding that only tiny gains are available.

unlaunched_prototype.formula: Zero below a frozen noise gate or for invalid results; otherwise clip((global_gain-noise)/median(prior valid positive global gains),0,1). If no such prior gains, first above-noise gain earns1.
unlaunched_prototype.proposed_history_scope: Only prior valid positive global-frontier gains whose measurements lie within the existing64-evaluation window; keep failed evaluations in window cost accounting.
unlaunched_prototype.noise_policy: No tolerance selected yet. Required explicit function argument; estimate/freeze from scheduled public training rereads before launch.
unlaunched_prototype.integration_status: Pure credit helper only. Not wired into engine, allocator, worker or automatic campaign launcher. No alternative policy evaluation performed.
unlaunched_prototype.limitations: Fractional credit would be pseudo-count evidence for the existing sampling rule, not a calibrated Bernoulli posterior. The scale can favor small improvements and reduce deep exploration; test as one-factor development ablation. No performance guarantee.
